chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the divorce of the deranged, he (peace be upon him) said: 'His guardian divorces on his behalf, for I consider him to be at the status of the Imam.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status of / in the position of

ai.seo_question: Who initiates divorce for an insane person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to establish that the guardian (*wali*) of the mentally incapacitated (*al-ma'tuh*) holds the authority to pronounce divorce on their behalf. The Imam’s declaration that the insane person is 'in the position of the Imam' highlights a key Shia juristic principle: just as the Imam represents the community in governance, the guardian represents the incapacitated individual in personal status law, ensuring their legal affairs are managed competently.
